data.name: Fulaihan
data.gender_notes: Fulaihan is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Fulaihan is derived from the Arabic word 'fil' which means 'gentle' or 'elegant'. The suffix 'ahan' means 'blossom' or 'flower'. So, Fulaihan means 'gentle blossom' or 'elegant flower'. The name Fulaihan carries the meaning “Gentle Blossom” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Fulaihan usually hope their child will grow to embody gentle blossom and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Fulaihan is a beautiful name with deep spiritual significance. It represents the gentle and delicate nature of Allah's creation. It is a reminder of the beauty and grace of nature and the importance of being gentle and kind to others.
data.etymology: Fulaihan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gentle Blossom.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fulaihan total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam, The History of the Conquests by the Moslems, Translated by H.F.A. Freeman-Kenyon. University of Chicago Press, 1966. p. 120-121.
historical_references.context: The name is mentioned in relation to the battle of Tudmir (711 AD), where Tarik ibn Ziyad defeated the Christian army under Roderic in the Battle of Guadalete. The name Fulaihan is mentioned as the name of the Muslim army commander who led the cavalry division.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Idhari, The Annals of the Muslim Conquests in Spain: Al-Futuh al-Andalusiyya, Translated by P.R. Kory. University of Pennsylvania Press, 1962. p. 43.
historical_references.context: The name is also mentioned in relation to the conquest of the city of Cordoba, where Musa ibn Nusayr sent Fulaihan as the governor.
